cause_quote: It made sendChatAction replaceable (`const replaceable = method === "sendChatAction" || callerScope?.replaceable === true`) and answered held-back replaceable calls with a synthetic 429 via `skippedFloodResponse(waitMs, "flood wait active")`, which the existing withTelegramApiErrorLogging wrapper around typing logs at ERROR.
user_saw: During a Telegram flood wait, the Gateway log filled with ERROR lines 'telegram sendChatAction failed: ... (flood wait active; request not sent)' for typing actions OpenClaw deliberately skipped.
summary: Synthetic 429s for deliberately skipped replaceable Telegram updates now carry a distinct suffix, and withTelegramApiErrorLogging no longer logs them at ERROR.
reasoning: Blame of the removed lines points to bb6bb777af31 (#157349), whose diff adds skippedFloodResponse with the '; request not sent)' description and routes sendChatAction through the replaceable skip path; the typing call sites in bot-message-context.ts were already wrapped in withTelegramApiErrorLogging(operation: "sendChatAction"), so every skipped typing logged an ERROR from the day the hold-back feature shipped. The same PR intended a single WARN per flood, so the per-request ERROR is a defect of that introduction, not a later regression.
